title: Walk the quiet battlefield loop at Horseshoe Bend
description: A quiet loop crosses the Horseshoe Bend battlefield while signs explain the landscape and its contested history.

title: Land on the Arctic dunes of Kobuk Valley
description: Bush planes reach the Great Kobuk Sand Dunes; once down, there are no trails or developed facilities.

title: Thread the rock pinnacles on Echo Canyon Loop
description: Echo Canyon Loop threads between Chiricahua’s rhyolite pinnacles on a rugged route mapped by the park.

title: Walk among the Plum Bayou earthworks
description: Trails circle Plum Bayou’s ceremonial mounds and plaza, with archaeological interpretation at the visitor centre.

title: Take a first lava-tube walk in Mushpot Cave
description: Mushpot offers a self-guided introduction to Lava Beds’ tubes, with cave hazards checked before entry.

title: Find ancient stumps on the Petrified Forest Loop
description: The Petrified Forest Loop passes Florissant’s fossil stumps in open montane country.

title: Walk from an artist’s farm to Weir Pond
description: Weir Pond Trail leaves the historic studios for the woodland and pond that shaped the artists’ setting.

title: Hike the Brandywine woods at Beaver Valley
description: Beaver Valley’s woodland paths reveal a rural corner of First State National Historical Park.

title: Watch lotus and wetland birds at Kenilworth
description: Kenilworth’s boardwalk links cultivated aquatic gardens with tidal wetland habitat inside Washington.

title: Cross the inlet to compact Fort Matanzas
description: A small ferry crosses the inlet to Fort Matanzas, so the fort visit depends on current boat operations.

title: Step inside Ocmulgee’s reconstructed Earth Lodge
description: Inside Ocmulgee’s reconstructed Earth Lodge, the clay floor is an original survival from the ancient council chamber.

title: Follow the lava shore to Kaloko Fishpond
description: Kaloko’s immense dry-stacked seawall shows how Native Hawaiian fishpond engineering worked with the tides.

title: Walk the quieter granite trails at City of Rocks
description: City of Rocks’ maintained footpaths wind between granite fins and emigrant-landmark formations.

title: Read labour history across Pullman’s factory town
description: Pullman’s factory grounds connect an ambitious planned community with the labour conflict embedded in its streets.

title: Enter the riverside rotunda at Vincennes
description: The Vincennes rotunda interprets George Rogers Clark’s Revolutionary campaign beside the Wabash River.

title: Walk the restored prairie at Herbert Hoover’s birthplace
description: Restored tallgrass surrounds Hoover’s birthplace, adding an ecological walk to the compact historic site.

title: Trace Black homesteading history in Nicodemus
description: A township walk links Nicodemus’ surviving buildings to the history of Black homesteaders on the plains.

title: Walk the open-air mining story at Blue Heron
description: Blue Heron preserves a coal community as an outdoor exhibit of structures, stories and former mine life.

title: Walk the layered grounds of Oakland Plantation
description: Oakland’s buildings and grounds hold intertwined histories of plantation owners, enslaved people and later workers.

title: Hear the Wabanaki and French story above Saint Croix Island
description: A shore trail overlooks Saint Croix Island while interpreting both Wabanaki presence and the early French settlement.

title: Find the Civil War batteries at Fort Foote
description: Wooded paths at Fort Foote lead to surviving earthworks and river-defence batteries south of Washington.

title: See an early ironworks turn by water power
description: Reconstructed furnaces, forge and waterwheels make early iron production tangible at Saugus.

title: Read copper-country history above Hancock
description: Quincy’s hillside retains shafts, hoist buildings and smelting history; partner tours vary by season.

title: Circle the pipestone quarries with cultural context
description: Pipestone’s short Circle Trail links prairie, quarry features and a living Indigenous cultural landscape.

title: Walk the compact Brices Cross Roads battlefield
description: The compact Brices Cross Roads landscape makes the battlefield’s movements legible without a long driving tour.

title: Follow George Washington Carver’s woodland trail
description: Carver Trail crosses the woods and fields of George Washington Carver’s childhood landscape.

title: Watch ranch history stay practical at Grant-Kohrs
description: Grant-Kohrs keeps ranch history practical through preserved work buildings and live demonstrations.

title: Climb past fossilised spiral burrows at Agate
description: The Daemonelix Trail climbs to corkscrew-shaped fossil burrows preserved in Nebraska’s prairie bluffs.

title: Walk a desert wash rich in Ice Age clues
description: Tule Springs has undeveloped desert routes, where careful walking protects exposed Ice Age fossil resources.

title: Walk between sculpture and woodland at Saint-Gaudens
description: Saint-Gaudens combines an artist’s home and studios with sculpture placed throughout quiet garden grounds.

title: Trace water power beside Paterson Great Falls
description: Paterson’s falls and old raceways show how river power drove one of America’s earliest industrial cities.

title: Walk Quarai’s Spanish Corral Trail beyond the mission
description: The one-mile dirt loop leaves Quarai’s main ruins for piñon-juniper woodland, native plant stories and the stone remains known as the Spanish Corral.

title: Leave the house tour for Sagamore Hill’s salt marsh
description: Sagamore Hill’s nature trail slips beyond the historic house through woodland to a salt marsh.

title: Cross the reconstructed bridge at Moores Creek
description: Moores Creek’s short path crosses a reconstructed bridge and follows the compact Revolutionary battlefield.

title: Enter a reconstructed Hidatsa earthlodge
description: The reconstructed earthlodge at Knife River introduces Hidatsa village architecture through a place visitors can enter.

title: Tour Colonel Charles Young’s preserved home
description: Charles Young’s preserved home gives a focused account of a pioneering Black officer and the Buffalo Soldiers.

title: Walk the sombre Washita battlefield trail
description: Washita’s walking trail treats the 1868 attack as a sombre landscape for learning and reflection.

title: Follow a ranger into the marble Oregon Caves
description: A ranger-led route enters Oregon’s marble caves; stairs, low passages and seasonal bookings shape the visit.

title: Step into the tavern at Allegheny Portage Railroad
description: The Lemon House restores the tavern that served travellers transferring across the Allegheny Portage Railroad.

title: See early textile power at Old Slater Mill
description: Old Slater Mill places water-powered textile machinery inside the Blackstone Valley’s industrial story.

title: Walk the siege trench to Ninety Six Star Fort
description: A trail and surviving siege trench lead to Ninety Six’s distinctive earthen Star Fort.

title: Tour a preserved Minuteman launch-control site
description: Small guided groups descend into Delta-01, a preserved Minuteman launch-control facility.

title: Look into the Obed gorge from Lilly Bluff
description: A short path reaches Lilly Bluff for a broad view into the forested Obed gorge.

title: Stand above an in-situ mammoth nursery herd
description: Waco’s dig shelter lets visitors stand above Columbian mammoth remains still preserved where they were found.

title: Climb to a ranger-led Timpanogos cave tour
description: The Timpanogos visit combines a steep mountain approach with a reserved ranger-led cave tour.

title: Walk the wooded carriage roads above Woodstock
description: Historic carriage roads form a quiet walking network through the managed forest above Woodstock.

title: Tour Maggie Walker’s Jackson Ward home
description: A guided visit to Maggie Walker’s Jackson Ward home connects domestic rooms with her civil-rights leadership.

title: Walk the military and boarding-school layers of Fort Spokane
description: Fort Spokane’s grounds carry two difficult layers: a military post and a later Indian boarding school.

title: Walk the near-empty rail streets of Thurmond
description: Thurmond’s depot and near-empty rail streets preserve the scale of a former New River boom town.

title: Climb an Ice Age Trail spur to Gibraltar Rock
description: This Ice Age Trail segment climbs through woods to Gibraltar Rock’s sandstone overlook.

title: Walk Fort Laramie beyond the parade ground
description: Beyond Fort Laramie’s parade ground, restored buildings reveal everyday life at the frontier post.

title: Pause in the memorial garden at La Paz
description: La Paz’s small memorial garden holds César and Helen Chávez’s graves and honours the farmworker movement.

title: Begin Tubman’s Eastern Shore story in the landscape
place: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad visitor trail
description: The visitor centre anchors Tubman’s story in the marshes, farms and waterways of Maryland’s Eastern Shore.

title: Listen and reflect at Sand Creek Massacre
description: Sand Creek’s overlook is a place to learn from Cheyenne and Arapaho history and reflect on the massacre.

title: Walk the remains of Minidoka incarceration camp
description: Minidoka’s walking route crosses surviving features of the Japanese American incarceration camp.

title: Walk the hoodoos with Indigenous cultural context
description: Writing-on-Stone pairs hoodoo trails with an Indigenous rock-art landscape that requires respectful interpretation.

title: Walk the river lots and church at Batoche
description: Batoche’s trails, church and river-lot landscape place Métis history back on the ground where it unfolded.

title: Hike Pukaskwa’s coast to the White River bridge
description: Pukaskwa’s demanding coastal day hike reaches a suspension bridge above the White River gorge.

title: Land among limestone monoliths in Mingan
description: Local boats land on Mingan islands where erosion has shaped freestanding limestone monoliths.

title: Cross to the preserved Roosevelt summer cottage
description: Campobello’s preserved Roosevelt cottage and grounds retain the scale of a family summer retreat.

title: Join a guided Mi’kmaq petroglyph walk at Kejimkujik
description: A guided Kejimkujik walk provides culturally respectful access to Mi’kmaq petroglyphs not open for casual viewing.

title: Cross the floating boardwalk into Greenwich dunes
description: Greenwich’s trail crosses a floating boardwalk before entering Prince Edward Island’s dune system.

title: Read Basque whaling history beside Red Bay harbour
description: Red Bay’s exhibits and archaeology reconstruct the Basque whaling station that operated on this Labrador harbour.

title: Walk tundra trails from Tombstone’s interpretive centre
description: Short tundra trails begin near Tombstone’s interpretive centre; backcountry plans require a separate level of preparation.

title: Walk between stelae deep in Calakmul’s forest
description: Calakmul’s plazas, structures and many stelae emerge from a forest setting far from Mexico’s busiest Maya circuit.

title: Climb Yagul’s terraces above the Tlacolula Valley
description: Yagul spreads palaces, murals and a ballcourt across a steep hill above the Tlacolula Valley.

title: Read desert architecture in the walls of Paquimé
description: Paquimé’s earthen walls and planned spaces trace trade between northern desert cultures and Mesoamerica.

title: Approach Cañada de la Virgen with its required guide
place: Cañada de la Virgen archaeological zone
description: Cañada de la Virgen is reached through controlled local transport and a walk to its astronomical ceremonial structures.

title: Cross volcanic desert to El Pinacate’s crater overlooks
description: El Pinacate’s route crosses a protected volcanic desert of craters, lava and immense dune fields.

title: Walk the rounded plazas of Huastec Tamtoc
description: Tamtoc’s rounded buildings and central plaza reveal a substantial Huastec settlement near Tamuín.

title: Walk between organ-pipe cliffs in Sierra de Órganos
description: Sierra de Órganos’ trails enter a protected valley of narrow, organ-pipe rock towers.

title: Find the sun shaft inside Xochicalco’s observatory cave
description: Xochicalco’s hilltop city includes a rock-cut observatory where sunlight enters through a vertical shaft.

title: Walk the curved yácata platforms at Tzintzuntzan
description: Tzintzuntzan’s broad platform carries the curved yácata structures of the former Purépecha capital.
